correctness.rationale: Both graphs have 16 vertices and 48 edges. An induced edge matching is a clique in the 48-vertex compatibility graph C_G. Independent rebuilding gives C_R with 216 edges and no triangles, so F_R(z)=1+48z+216z^2; the maximum-exchange graph is its line graph, has 216 vertices, degree 16, 1728 edges and exhaustive BFS diameter 3. C_S has 192 edges, 32 triangles and no 4-cliques, giving F_S(z)=1+48z+192z^2+32z^3; every compatible-pair lies in at most one triple, hence its 32 maximum triples have no one-edge exchanges. Exact direct 48-edge enumerations and exchange BFS verify every finite case rather than relying on stored output.

evidence: Beezer–Farrell 2000 already distinguishes the same graphs by ordinary matching polynomials, and generalized graph-complex methods do not directly yield optimum edge exchange diameter.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing general descriptions of line graphs and strongly regular parameters provide a computation recipe, not the stated explicit induced matching counts and exchange geometry.

value.rationale: Complete induced-edge-matching enumerators and exact local-search mobility for the canonical pair of cospectral nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs. A substantive and natural contrast: optimal size differs and optimum exchange goes from a connected diameter-three graph to isolated configurations. Fixed finite cases are a natural distinguished benchmark, not an arbitrary graph slice.

limitations: Only the two 16-vertex examples; no universal strongly-regular graph theorem.
residual_risks: The 2026 Shrikhande monograph was not inspected in full and may encode overlapping fixed-graph tables.
Diameter 3 is established by bounded exhaustive BFS, not a conceptual uniform diameter formula.
